question: A shirt is marked at ₹800. A shopkeeper offers a discount of 25% on it. What is the selling price of the shirt after the discount?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A 25% discount means the item is sold at 100% − 25% = 75% of its Marked Price.

Selling Price = 75% of MP = 3/4 × MP

Selling Price = 3/4 × 800 = 600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹800

Discount = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

Discount = (Discount% ÷ 100) × MP

 
 Marked Price
 ₹800
 
 

 

 − 25% Discount

 
 Selling Price
 ₹600
 
 Discount = 25% of ₹800 = ₹200

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount amount = (25 ÷ 100) × 800

⇒ Discount amount = 0.25 × 800 = ₹200

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

⇒ SP = 800 − 200 = ₹600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

It is the printed or tag price of an article. Discounts are always calculated on the Marked Price.

Successive Discount

If two successive discounts of x% and y% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by: [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%.

Selling Price vs Cost Price

Profit or loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP), whereas the discount is deducted from the Marked Price (MP) to get the Selling Price (SP).
